subject.title: [Feature]: Support plugin-requestable session isolation for trust boundaries

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public Plugin SDK/runtime API that lets plugins request sandboxed session execution and receive enforceable provenance/trust metadata, or keep isolation as operator-configured sessions_spawn/agent policy only?
rationale: The request changes a public plugin contract and could create a new security-boundary promise, so automation cannot safely choose the API shape or guarantee level.

options.title: Design additive isolation contract
options.body: Keep this open as the design track and specify sandbox requirements, tool constraints, provenance metadata, failure handling, and compatibility after the prerequisite hook-context issues are settled.

options.title: Document current operator pattern
options.body: Decline a new plugin-returned directive for now and document reader-agent plus sessions_spawn sandbox="require" as the supported workaround for untrusted content processing.

options.title: Defer until prerequisites land
options.body: Leave the proposal parked until the hook enrichment and durable-state policy surfaces are accepted or rejected, then revisit the isolation API.

recommendation.title: Design additive isolation contract
recommendation.body: Keep this open as the design track and specify sandbox requirements, tool constraints, provenance metadata, failure handling, and compatibility after the prerequisite hook-context issues are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: The current hook/subagent source lines and recent subagent history point to Peter as the strongest available routing candidate for the runtime/security-boundary choice.
